elements.label: Figure 7.7
elements.title: Neural Network with Loss Function
elements.details: Diagram shows a flow from independent variables W and B (weights and biases) feeding into a Neural Network box, which also takes input data x^(0) (as constants). The Neural Network outputs ŷ, which is compared with actual output data y (as constants) via a loss function C, resulting in Loss = z. The flow is W, B -> Neural Network -> ŷ -> C (with y) -> Loss = z.
elements.summary: This diagram illustrates how a neural network uses weights and biases along with input data to produce a prediction, which is then compared to actual output data via a loss function to compute the loss.

elements.label: Figure 7.8
elements.title: Simple Application of Gradient Descent
elements.details: 3D surface plot showing loss z as a function of weight w and bias b. Axes: w (weight) from -1.1 to 1.1, b (bias) from -1.1 to 1, z (loss) from approximately -0.02 to 0.78. The point (w=0.5, b=0.25) is marked with loss z=0.46. An arrow indicates the direction of steepest descent from this point on the surface.
elements.summary: This 3D plot visualizes the loss surface with respect to weight and bias, highlighting the point (0.5, 0.25) with loss 0.46 and showing the direction of steepest descent used in gradient descent optimization.
